verdicts.quote: Default schedule `[-3, 0, 7, 14]`, send time `09:00`. Offsets are days from the due date: three days before, on the due date, then 7 and 14 days after.
once an invoice is paid in full, voided, cancelled or written off, no further reminder is sent for it. ... A partial payment does not stop reminders.
verdicts.missing: Credited invoices and payment plans are not addressed; disputed/hold states are explicitly out of scope and left open (R-3 Boundaries, G-3).

verdicts.quote: The offset 0 mail states an outstanding balance of `850.00 USD`, not 1,250.00.
Unresolved: legal or consent obligations such as an opt-out footer, and a retention period (G-7). They are not assumed either way.
verdicts.missing: Whether an existing do-not-contact, paused or unsubscribed customer state suppresses reminders, and whether billing notices are exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: for one invoice and one step offset at most one reminder is sent, however many evaluations overlap, repeat, restart or retry.
The invoice's status and balance are read from the host immediately before each send. If it became ineligible after the step was claimed, no mail is sent

Transient provider failure or an unreadable host → record `Retrying`. Later evaluations try again while ... the next step's moment has not arrived. ... Out of scope: alerts, dashboards, e-mail to the operator about failures.
Quotas. The mail provider's rate and daily limits are unknown (G-2). The spec sets none and invents none.
verdicts.missing: How a large batch is paced within the provider's rate limit and what happens when the limit is hit.

verdicts.quote: A step is sendable only if its scheduled moment is not before the latest of: (a) the moment the current configuration was saved ... Reason: switching reminders on must not email every long-overdue customer at once.
There is also a send time of day (24-hour `HH:MM`) and a timezone (IANA name). ... A step's moment is its date at the send time in that timezone.
verdicts.missing: The timezone is a single business setting, not the customer's local time; weekends and holidays are not addressed.

verdicts.quote: Dates are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Amounts are `1,250.00 USD`.
No billing email → no mail. The record is `Skipped(no_recipient)`. ... Permanent rejection (invalid address, refused recipient) → `Failed(rejected)`, never retried.
the mail goes to the invoice's billing email and nowhere else.
verdicts.missing: What happens when the customer has several billing contacts, and which one(s) receive the reminder.

verdicts.quote: for each invoice an authorised operator can see, one row per handled step: offset, scheduled moment, outcome ..., time of last change, attempt count, and the address used.

It states the business name, customer name, invoice number, outstanding balance with currency, the due date ... If the host's invoice already carries payment instructions or a link, they are included (G-4).
verdicts.missing: Whether a way to pay is guaranteed in the reminder (left open in G-4) and whether any payment link expires.

verdicts.quote: Operator authority = whoever the host already lets manage billing settings. No new roles.
an authorised operator can turn automatic reminders On or Off. ... Out of scope: a "send backlog now" action, and per-customer or per-invoice switches
verdicts.missing: Previewing or dry-running what would be sent is not stated; manual resend is only excluded by R-4's out-of-scope list.

verdicts.quote: Consumer outcome: the operator can see which customers were not reached and why.
verdicts.missing: No view of upcoming or next scheduled reminders; history shows only steps already handled.

verdicts.quote: How late after a step's moment a reminder may be sent is not stated by the request. No number is invented.
verdicts.missing: An actual lateness bound or sending-volume cap; both N-1 and N-4 are left unresolved (G-8).

verdicts.quote: Invoice data (status, balance, due date, issue time, billing email) | Host invoice system. This feature never writes it.
